The candidate now ships 47 of its own tests, including the geometry identities and a two-rank NCCL run that completes three steps with find_unused_parameters=False. The mechanism is one connected pathway: the training-only successor attraction weights the tangent direction of the Frechet codebook step and the same weights sit inside the commitment term, with both switches present in the code and only the both-on arm trained. behavioral_evidence.claim: the proposed training-only signal
behavioral_evidence.value: Popularity-adjusted directed-transition centrality of each item (a parameter-free, normalized successor/predecessor flow), used as the per-item weight inside the code estimation.

behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: From the frozen split files, take only the Stage-3 TRAINING interaction sequences (the same prefix used to train the generative recommender), after the frozen dedup/filtering. For each consecutive pair (x_t, x_{t+1}) in a training sequence increment n(x -> y). Normalize with no free exponent: n_hat(x->y) = n(x->y) / sqrt(d_out(x) * d_in(y)), with d_out(x) = sum_y n(x->y) and d_in(y) = sum_x n(x->y). Item mass mu(x) = sum_y n_hat(x->y) + sum_z n_hat(z->x). Then mu_tilde(x) = mu(x) / mean over training items, clipped at the empirical 99th percentile, and w(x) = 1 + log1p(mu_tilde(x)); items with no training transition get mu = 0 hence w = 1. The table is computed once, before Stage-2 training starts, and is a read-only lookup during training.

behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak
behavioral_evidence.value: The transition table is built exclusively from the Stage-3 training sequences; validation and test interactions are removed from the file before any counting, so no validation/test co-occurrence, popularity or ordering can influence a weight. Items that appear only in validation/test are absent from the table and receive w = 1; they are never dropped and their SIDs come from the frozen Stage-2 item features alone. SID construction is therefore a deterministic function of (frozen Stage-2 item features, Stage-3 training transitions) only; the same frozen SID table is used for all three splits; and since there is no early stopping and no arm selection, no validation quantity ever feeds back into the SID.

geometric_necessity.value: Unit negative curvature (c = 1) Poincare ball with Mobius addition, metric factor lambda_u = 2/(1 - c||u||^2), exponential and logarithmic maps exp_u / log_u, and geodesic distance d_c(u,v) = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c) ||(-u) (+) v||); the estimator is the Riemannian (Karcher) mean, i.e. repeated geodesic steps along the tangent-space average of log maps.

Inside the quantizer's code-vector estimation, at every Stage-2 step, for every level of the residual chain; it acts on how m_k is produced from the points assigned to k. The assignment step, the encoder, the decoder, the reconstruction and commitment terms, and all of Stage 3 are unchanged.

m_k <- exp^{c}_{m_k} ( eta_k * [ sum_{i in A_k} w(x_i) * log^{c}_{m_k}( p_i ) ] / [ sum_{i in A_k} w(x_i) ] ), with w(x_i) = 1 + log1p( mu_tilde(x_i) ), p_i = z_i/(||z_i|| + tau), and exp^c / log^c the curvature-c Poincare maps; the behaviour term is w(x_i), the curved term is (log^c, exp^c, lambda^c), and they multiply inside one gradient.

implementation_cost.value: Stage 2 is 3000 epochs x 24 steps = 72,000 steps at 24,556 items (~1023 items/step). behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed

The mechanism touches only Stage 2 (the RQ-VAE); the Stage 3 protocol and its split stay frozen, and the SID construction sees only the training graph, so no validation or test interaction can influence a code assignment.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: w[i,j] is set to 0 for all edges (the sampler returns a constant-zero weight). L_succ then has value mean(log 2) and exactly zero gradient, so the run reproduces the baseline RQ-VAE trajectory up to non-determinism. The switch exists in code and is correct; it is not run this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full term with row-normalised w[i,j] and Poincare d_kappa at the measured curvature -1/s^2, added to the unchanged RQ-VAE loss with weight 1 (dimensionless, because numerator and m0^2 share units). This is the only arm trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: kappa is disabled and d_kappa^2(u,v) is replaced in the same equation by ||zhat_i^(<=h) - zhat_j^(<=h)||^2 (Euclidean, with m0^2 recomputed as the Euclidean counterpart at epoch 0). Same sampler, same weights, same softplus, same prefix depths. Exists in code, not run.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the Stage 2 training split only. For every training session (ordered item list) and every adjacent pair (i_t, i_{t+1}) with both items in the 24556-item training vocabulary, increment T[i_t, i_{t+1}]. Then for each anchor i set w[i,j] = T[i,j] / max_{j'} T[i,j'], so w lies in (0,1] and the strongest successor of every anchor gets 1.0. N(i) = {j : T[i,j] > 0}. Anchors with out-degree 0 are excluded. The table is built once before training and is never rebuilt from model state.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item transitions with row-normalised strength, taken from consecutive co-consumption inside a training session, used as a per-edge weight and as a negative-sampling constraint.
ideas.cost_estimate: No extra forward passes and no extra encoder compute. Per step at the frozen scale: 1024 sampled transitions x 3 prefix depths x 2 distances (positive and negative) = 6144 Poincare distance evaluations at dimension d (64-128), about 0.5 MFLOP, plus 3 gather-sums over 3 tables per endpoint, i.e. under 0.5 percent of one optimizer step. Cache refresh is O(24556 x 3) integer writes once per epoch (72000 steps over 3000 epochs; 24 steps per epoch). Memory: 24556 x 3 int32 = 295 KB. Expected wall-clock delta on four cards: under 1 percent.
ideas.coupling_equation: L_succ = mean over sampled (i,j) of softplus( w[i,j] * [ D_ij - D_ijminus + m0^2 ] ), with D_ij = (1/3) * sum_{h in {1,2,L}} d_kappa^2( p_i^(h), p_j^(h) ), p_i^(h) = exp_0^kappa( sum_{l<=h} C_l[k_l(i)] ), and m0^2 the measured mean geodesic distance between random code pairs.
ideas.coupling_path: w[i,j] (behaviour) multiplies the softplus of a geodesic gap (geometry) computed on prefix code sums drawn from the codebook table; the resulting gradient is the only thing that moves the codebook away from its reconstruction optimum, so it is the single path by which both signals reach the SID. Setting w to zero removes every gradient of the term (behaviour-off is exactly the baseline trajectory); replacing d_kappa with the Euclidean norm changes the direction and scale of every codebook update while keeping the identical term structure (geometry-off). Neither substitution leaves the other intact, because w and d_kappa appear multiplied inside the same softplus argument.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the successor table carries usable structure at the granularity of code prefixes, then a behaviour-weighted geodesic margin on the codebook should raise the fraction of transitions whose successor shares the anchor's level-1 and level-2 code above the reconstruction-only baseline, and that gain should carry into Stage 3 test Recall@10 above 0.065 without any change to the Stage 3 protocol. Observed through: successor-prefix hit rate per level, codebook usage entropy, mean geodesic distance of true successor pairs versus random pairs, and finally Stage 3 test_recall@10 on the single run.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Entirely in the quantization stage, as a gradient on the shared codebook parameters C_1..C_L of the RQ-VAE. The encoder, the nearest-code assignment rule, the decoder, the commitment loss and the reconstruction loss are all unchanged.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Fixed negative curvature -kappa with kappa = 1/s^2 and s^2 = mean_i ||zhat_i||^2 measured at the end of epoch 0 and frozen. Operations: exp_0^kappa(v) = tanh(sqrt(kappa)||v||) * v / (sqrt(kappa)||v||) into the open unit ball, Moebius addition, and the Poincare distance d_kappa(u,v) = (2/sqrt(kappa)) * artanh(sqrt(kappa) * ||(-u) (+) v||).
ideas.key_change: After each epoch we snapshot every training item's L code indices (free: they come from the forward passes already run). Each step we sample training-only transitions, form prefix code sums at levels 1, 2 and L, map them by exp_0^kappa into a Poincare ball of fixed measured curvature -kappa, and apply a softplus triplet margin in which the positive/negative geodesic gap is multiplied by the transition weight; gradient flows into the codebooks only.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition table is built exclusively from training-split sessions; validation and test interactions are never read by the table builder, never enter the cache of code indices (filled only from training-item forward passes), and never appear as anchors, positives or negatives. Validation/test items absent from the training vocabulary are not in the cache, so they cannot enter the margin. The mechanism touches only Stage 2 (the RQ-VAE); the Stage 3 protocol and its split stay frozen, and the SID construction sees only the training graph, so no validation or test interaction can influence a code assignment.
ideas.motivation: RQ-VAE semantic IDs are built for reconstruction, not for transitions. Two items a user actually moves between often land on unrelated prefixes, so the generative recommender must memorise the transition instead of reading it off the code tree. The fix cannot be "add a graph loss", because a flat Euclidean graph loss just pulls code vectors together and collapses the codebook; the natural geometry for a tree-shaped prefix code with an exponentially growing frontier is negative curvature.
ideas.novelty: Prior rounds put curvature on the assignment (Sinkhorn / voronoi / curvature cells), on transported tangent frames (fork angle, shell, cone), or on anchored charts. This one leaves the assignment, the encoder and the Sinkhorn machinery completely untouched and puts the curved operation on the CODEBOOK UPDATE: a curvature-measured geodesic triplet margin over prefix-truncated code sums, with the margin violation weighted by a row-normalised transition strength. It is a code-table geometry, not an assignment geometry, not a transport, not a chart, and not an auxiliary hyperbolic head on the encoder.
ideas.observables: (a) successor-prefix hit rate at levels 1 and 2 versus baseline; (b) mean d_kappa for true successor pairs relative to random pairs (separation ratio); (c) codebook usage entropy and the number of exact L-code duplicates; (d) Stage 3 test_recall@10. All diagnostics are recorded, none is an admission gate; the single run's test_recall@10 decides.
risks: (a) Codebook-only gradient may be too slow to relocate codes within 3000 epochs, leaving SIDs close to baseline. (b) Negative sampling noise can pull unrelated items together when the table is sparse (cold items with one transition). (c) The margin can be satisfied by driving two items to identical codes, which would help the objective but destroy SID uniqueness and hurt generation; a duplicate-count diagnostic covers this. (d) If code sums sit very near the origin the derived curvature is too flat and Poincare distance degenerates toward Euclidean, so the coupling becomes numerically inert.
ideas.safeguards: (1) Clamp ||v|| before exp0 so the mapped radius stays below 1 - 1e-5 (tanh saturates to exactly 1 in float32). (2) Clamp the artanh argument to 1 - 1e-7 and compute d_kappa in float64. (3) If s2 <= 1e-12, fall back to kappa = 1 and log a warning instead of dividing by zero. (4) Guard s2, kappa and m0_sq so they are finite and positive; otherwise disable the term for the run and record the flag (no retuning). (5) Skip pairs with out_i = 0, with w = 0, or with an endpoint not yet in the cache; never let an unseen item contribute. (6) The negative must not be in N(i) and must differ from i and j; if all 5 resamples fail, drop the pair rather than use a false negative. (7) Record the L-code duplicate count each epoch so the collapse failure mode is visible (no extra repulsion term is added; that would be a different mechanism). (8) Force w[i,i] = 0. (9) Divide L_succ by the number of kept pairs so gradient magnitude does not drift with table density. (10) Freeze kappa after epoch 0 so curvature cannot drift toward zero and silently Euclideanise the term.

```
loss = 0; kept = 0
for (i,j) in S:
    jm = uniform item with T[i,jm] == 0 and jm not in {i,j}
         resample <= 5 times; if it fails, drop the pair
    D_pos = 0; D_neg = 0
    for h in (1,2,L):
        u   = exp0(sum_{l<=h} C_l[k_l(i)])
        D_pos += (1/3) * d_kappa^2(u, exp0(sum_{l<=h} C_l[k_l(j)]))
        D_neg += (1/3) * d_kappa^2(u, exp0(sum_{l<=h} C_l[k_l(jm)]))
    loss += softplus( w[i,j] * (D_pos - D_neg + m0_sq) );  kept += 1
L_total = L_RQVAE + loss / max(1, kept)
backward(); step()

# --- end of epoch ---
overwrite cache k_1..k_L for all 24556 training items with the argmin
indices produced by that epoch's forward passes (no extra forward pass)
# kappa and m0_sq are NEVER recomputed after epoch 0
```
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: the precomputed sparse transition table T and row-normalised weights w (training split only), the epoch cache of code indices k_l(i) for the 24556 training items, the shared codebook parameters C_1..C_L, and the two frozen scalars kappa and m0_sq measured at epoch 0. Output: the scalar L_succ and its gradient with respect to C_1..C_L only (the cached indices are integer constants, so no encoder gradient is taken through this path). It returns nothing else and does not modify assignment, decoding or the SID export.
ideas.title: Behaviour-weighted geodesic triplet margin that moves the shared RQ codebook table so successor items' hierarchical code prefixes are Poincare-close

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: A switch `use_behaviour_weights = False` that sets w(x) := 1 for all items, so g_k becomes the unweighted Karcher mean and the codebook is purely geometry-driven while every other line, including the curved estimator, is identical. Present and unit-checked in code; never trained.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full coupled run, `use_behaviour_weights = True` and `curvature_off = False`: behaviour-weighted Karcher estimation in the Poincare ball. This single run is the candidate; no arm is trained with either switch off.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: A switch `curvature_off = True` that replaces the Poincare log/exp with Euclidean subtraction/addition and sets lambda = 1, so the estimator becomes the ordinary weighted arithmetic centroid (w still applied) while the behaviour table and the assignment code path are identical. Present and unit-checked in code; never trained.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the frozen split files, take only the Stage-3 TRAINING interaction sequences (the same prefix used to train the generative recommender), after the frozen dedup/filtering. For each consecutive pair (x_t, x_{t+1}) in a training sequence increment n(x -> y). Normalize with no free exponent: n_hat(x->y) = n(x->y) / sqrt(d_out(x) * d_in(y)), with d_out(x) = sum_y n(x->y) and d_in(y) = sum_x n(x->y). Item mass mu(x) = sum_y n_hat(x->y) + sum_z n_hat(z->x). Then mu_tilde(x) = mu(x) / mean over training items, clipped at the empirical 99th percentile, and w(x) = 1 + log1p(mu_tilde(x)); items with no training transition get mu = 0 hence w = 1. The table is computed once, before Stage-2 training starts, and is a read-only lookup during training.
ideas.behavior_signal: Popularity-adjusted directed-transition centrality of each item (a parameter-free, normalized successor/predecessor flow), used as the per-item weight inside the code estimation.
ideas.cost_estimate: Stage 2 is 3000 epochs x 24 steps = 72,000 steps at 24,556 items (~1023 items/step). Per step the update touches 3 levels x ~1023 points x d=64: about 2e5 elementwise ops (two Mobius additions, one artanh, one tanh per point-level), fully vectorised, well under 1 ms on one GPU against a typical 50-150 ms encoder step, i.e. an estimated +1 to +3 percent Stage-2 wall clock, roughly +2 to +5 minutes over the whole 72,000 steps. One-off preprocessing: counting training transitions (a few million pairs) plus one forward pass over 24,556 items to measure tau: about 1 to 2 minutes. Stage 3 cost is exactly zero (it consumes integer SIDs). No extra epochs, no extra forward or backward passes, no extra parameters.
ideas.coupling_equation: m_k <- exp^{c}_{m_k} ( eta_k * [ sum_{i in A_k} w(x_i) * log^{c}_{m_k}( p_i ) ] / [ sum_{i in A_k} w(x_i) ] ), with w(x_i) = 1 + log1p( mu_tilde(x_i) ), p_i = z_i/(||z_i|| + tau), and exp^c / log^c the curvature-c Poincare maps; the behaviour term is w(x_i), the curved term is (log^c, exp^c, lambda^c), and they multiply inside one gradient.
ideas.coupling_path: mu(x) [training transitions] -> w(x) -> weighted tangent mean g_k = sum_i w_i log_{m_k}(p_i)/sum_i w_i -> geodesic step m_k <- exp_{m_k}(eta_k g_k) -> codebook positions -> nearest-code assignment -> SID tokens -> Stage-3 prefix statistics. Removing the behaviour term makes g_k an unweighted Karcher mean; removing curvature (Euclidean log/exp, lambda = 1) makes it an ordinary weighted arithmetic centroid. Either removal changes the codebook, hence the SIDs.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If within-cell transition mass is strongly heterogeneous (heavy-tailed popularity gives mu_tilde coefficients of variation well above 1 inside most cells) and the hyperbolic Karcher mean materially relocates codes, then hub-adjacent items get finer effective resolution and SID prefixes become more behaviourally predictable, lifting Stage 3 test Recall@10 above 0.065 in the single coupled run. It is worth keeping if that run exceeds 0.065 AND the logged diagnostics confirm the mechanism actually fired (weight dispersion and code displacement are non-trivial); it is not worth keeping if recall does not move even though the diagnostics show the coupling was active, or if recall moves while the diagnostics show the weights were nearly uniform.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the quantizer's code-vector estimation, at every Stage-2 step, for every level of the residual chain; it acts on how m_k is produced from the points assigned to k. The assignment step, the encoder, the decoder, the reconstruction and commitment terms, and all of Stage 3 are unchanged.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Unit negative curvature (c = 1) Poincare ball with Mobius addition, metric factor lambda_u = 2/(1 - c||u||^2), exponential and logarithmic maps exp_u / log_u, and geodesic distance d_c(u,v) = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c) ||(-u) (+) v||); the estimator is the Riemannian (Karcher) mean, i.e. repeated geodesic steps along the tangent-space average of log maps.
ideas.key_change: Replace the quantizer's Euclidean code-vector update (EMA centroid or gradient step) by a single Riemannian Karcher step in the Poincare ball, with each assigned residual point reweighted by a popularity-adjusted transition centrality of its item. Assignment code path, encoder, decoder, loss and Stage 3 are untouched.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition table is built exclusively from the Stage-3 training sequences; validation and test interactions are removed from the file before any counting, so no validation/test co-occurrence, popularity or ordering can influence a weight. Items that appear only in validation/test are absent from the table and receive w = 1; they are never dropped and their SIDs come from the frozen Stage-2 item features alone. SID construction is therefore a deterministic function of (frozen Stage-2 item features, Stage-3 training transitions) only; the same frozen SID table is used for all three splits; and since there is no early stopping and no arm selection, no validation quantity ever feeds back into the SID.
ideas.motivation: Every existing curved-SID mechanism moves the *assignment* (curved cost, Sinkhorn, cones, shells) or the *residual* (transport), while leaving the estimator untouched: a code vector is still a Euclidean centroid of its assigned points. Consequence: a code is pulled by the raw item cloud, so behaviourally central items (the ones that actually determine what follows what) get exactly as much say in the code position as dead-tail items that merely happen to land in the same cell. Behaviourally coherent prefixes therefore stay diluted, and the generative recommender is asked to predict tokens whose geometry was never shaped by transitions.
ideas.novelty: The curved operation is placed on the code-vector *estimator*, not on the cost. Each code is computed as a behaviour-weighted Frechet (Karcher) mean in the Poincare ball, so (i) the behaviour signal changes which assigned points dominate the code, and (ii) curvature changes how those dominant points pull (hyperbolic log maps grow like log((1+r)/(1-r)), and the Karcher mean contracts toward the ball centre relative to the Euclidean mean). No previous arm in this programme estimated codes geodesically; nothing here reuses a Sinkhorn cost, a tangent-space fork transport, a radial shell/volume scalar, a margin/cone, or a per-node curvature field.
ideas.observables: (1) the fraction of the 24,556 items whose level-0 (and level-1) code differs from the code the Euclidean uniform estimator would have produced on the same assignments; (2) dispersion of w inside each cell (per-code coefficient of variation of mu_tilde) and per-code weighted mass versus item count, i.e. whether hub-heavy cells absorb more items; (3) mean geodesic Karcher step size ||eta_k g_k|| per level over epochs, and the radial distribution of codes (checking that codes do not all collapse toward the origin); (4) prefix behaviour predictability: on training-only sequences, the conditional entropy / top-1 accuracy of the next item's level-k code given the previous codes, compared against the frozen baseline SID table; (5) Stage-3 test Recall@10, the judgement.
risks: The 99th-percentile clip could still let a handful of hub items dominate a cell, collapsing several codes toward the same region and creating prefix collisions. The hyperbolic mean contracts codes toward the ball centre, which may crowd many codes into the inner region and destroy the radial spread the frozen quantizer relied on. Long-tail data may make mu_tilde nearly uniform for the bulk of items so the mechanism barely fires. If the frozen quantizer already assigns under a hyperbolic metric, the interaction with a curved estimator may be redundant or unstable. A single run cannot separate a real gain from seed noise, so a marginal improvement (e.g. 0.0655) is not evidence.
ideas.safeguards: Compute all norms with an epsilon of 1e-8 in denominators; verify after each update that max_k ||m_k|| <= 1 - 1e-5 and clamp radially if floating point ever violates it (the exp map is contractive so this is a numerical guard, not a mechanism); clip the tangent vector norm ||g_k|| at 1e3 before the exp map to avoid an artanh/tanh overflow on degenerate batches; skip cells with |A_k| = 0; skip a whole update and log a warning if any non-finite value appears in m_k (never write NaN into the codebook); compute the chart with tau floored at 1e-6; initialise codes at the chart images of the frozen Euclidean init so the geometry-off and both-on runs start from identical code vectors; keep the update in float32 and run the Mobius/log/exp arithmetic in a fixed order (no reordering that changes summation) so the run is reproducible; assert at start-up that w == 1 exactly when the behaviour switch is off and that log/exp round-trip (exp_u(log_u(v)) ~= v within 1e-4) when curvature is on.
ideas.spec_equations:
Precompute once (CPU, before training):
  tau := median_{x in Stage2train} ||z_x||                      # one forward pass, 24,556 items
  chart: p(z) := z / (||z|| + tau)                               # p in ball, ||p|| < 1
  transitions n(x->y) from Stage-3 TRAIN sequences only
  n_hat(x->y) := n(x->y) / sqrt(d_out(x) d_in(y)), d_out(x)=sum_y n(x->y), d_in(y)=sum_x n(x->y)
  mu(x) := sum_y n_hat(x->y) + sum_z n_hat(z->x)
  mu_tilde(x) := mu(x) / mean(mu), then clip at quantile_0.99(mu)
  w(x) := 1 + log1p(mu_tilde(x))                                # w == 1 iff behaviour switched off
Poincare primitives, c = 1:
  mobius(u,v) := ((1 + 2c<u,v> + c||v||^2) u + (1 - c||u||^2) v) / (1 + 2c<u,v> + c^2||u||^2||v||^2)
  lam(u)      := 2 / (1 - c||u||^2)
  log_u(v)    := (2/(sqrt(c) lam(u))) * artanh(sqrt(c)||mobius(-u,v)||) * mobius(-u,v)/max(||mobius(-u,v)||, eps)
  exp_u(t)    := mobius(u, tanh(sqrt(c) lam(u)||t||/2) * t / max(sqrt(c)||t||, eps))
Per Stage-2 step, for each level l (codes m_k already in the ball), after the frozen forward pass gives assignments A_k and residual points z_i:
  p_i := p(z_i)
  for k with A_k non-empty:
      g_k := sum_{i in A_k} w(x_i) * log_{m_k}(p_i) / sum_{i in A_k} w(x_i)
      eta_k := 1 / (1 + N_k)                       # N_k = raw count of assignments to k, accumulated
      m_k := exp_{m_k}( eta_k * g_k )              # stays in the ball for any finite g_k
  N_k := N_k + |A_k|
  write m_k back as the codebook entry, then continue with the frozen loss and backward pass.
Geometry-off variant: log_u(v) := v - u, exp_u(t) := u + t, lam := 1, chart p(z) := z.
Behaviour-off variant: w := 1.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: the frozen Stage-2 item latent z_i produced by the encoder for the current batch (reset points per level), the current codebook matrices {m_k} in chart coordinates, the per-item weight table w (24,556 floats), the accumulated assignment counts N_k, and the two switches. Outputs: updated codebook matrices {m_k} in the ball, updated N_k, and per-step scalars for the diagnostics (mean ||eta_k g_k||, per-code weight dispersion, fraction of cells touched). The operator returns nothing else; it does not alter logits, assignments, or gradients.

specification.text: Chart the latent: p = z/(||z||+tau), tau = median ||z|| measured once over the frozen 24,556 Stage-2 items; curvature c = 1 (unit negative curvature, ball radius 1). For each level l and each code k with assigned points p_i and item weights w_i: g_k = sum_i w_i * log_{m_k}(p_i) / sum_i w_i ; m_k <- exp_{m_k}( eta_k * g_k ) ; eta_k = 1/(1+N_k) with N_k the raw (unweighted) assignment count. Behaviour enters only through w_i; geometry enters only through log/exp and the metric factor lambda. w_i = 1 + log1p( mu_tilde(x_i) ) where mu_tilde is the transition-centrality normalized to mean 1 and clipped at its data 99th percentile.

ideas.title: Behaviour-mass weighted Karcher (Poincare) codebook estimation for the RQ-VAE semantic-ID quantizer.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: g_i is replaced by the constant 0.5 for every item, so the metric is the unweighted normalised product distance and the Karcher step is unweighted; the code still exists and is exercised by one config flag, but no such run is trained this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the full mechanism above: behaviour-gated mixed-curvature assignment plus behaviour-gated Karcher codebook, trained once on the frozen 3000-epoch Stage-2 budget and evaluated with the frozen Stage-3 protocol, with no early stopping, no sweep and no seed repetition.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: k_H and k_S are driven to 0, so exp0/log0 become the identity, p = zhat_H, q = zhat_S, A and B are unbounded Euclidean points, and D_ik = sqrt(g_i * (||p - A||/D_Hmax)^2 + (1-g_i) * (||q - B||/D_Smax)^2); this is the plain behaviour-weighted Euclidean RQ-VAE and is not trained this round.
ideas.behavior_computation: From every Stage-2 training sequence, count edges u_t -> u_{t+1}; for each item i collect its out-neighbour set N_i and count edges among N_i; C_i = c_i/(k_i(k_i-1)); g_i = clip(1 - C_i, 0.1, 0.9), with g_i = 0.5 when k_i < 5. Computed once before Stage 2 starts and frozen for all 3000 epochs.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item transitions from the Stage-2 training sequences only, reduced to a per-item directed local clustering coefficient (cycle/lateral mass among an item's own successors).
ideas.cost_estimate: No new parameters of consequence (3 x 256 x d product codebook points, plus the 24556-vector g). One-time graph pass over the training transitions, O(E) with E = number of consecutive pairs (order 10^6), a few seconds and a 24556-element output. Per step at the frozen scale only 24556/24 ~= 1023 items are quantized against 3 x 256 codes, i.e. ~7.9e5 product distances per step, each costing one arcosh plus one arccos over d-dimension inner products; this is roughly 3-5x the baseline Euclidean squared-distance kernel, which is itself a sub-millisecond, launch-bound slice of a Stage-2 step, so the expected per-step overhead is well under 1% of a Stage-2 step and under 2-3% of total wall clock over 3000 x 24 = 72000 steps. Memory overhead is negligible. No sweep, no extra seed, no extra arm: one training run.
ideas.coupling_equation: D_ik = sqrt( g_i * (d_H^{k_H}(p_i, A_lk) / D_Hmax)^2 + (1 - g_i) * (d_S^{k_S}(q_i, B_lk) / D_Smax)^2 ), with g_i = clip(1 - C_i(N_i^{train}), 0.1, 0.9), d_H = (1/sqrt(k_H)) arcosh(1 + 2 k_H ||p-a||^2 / ((1 - k_H||p||^2)(1 - k_H||a||^2))), d_S = R_S arccos(clip(<q,b>/R_S^2, -1+1e-6, 1-1e-6)), and the codebook step A_lk <- exp0^{k_H}( sum_i s_ik g_i log0^{k_H}(p_i) / sum_i s_ik g_i ).
ideas.coupling_path: g_i is computed from training transitions, then multiplies the squared normalised Poincare distance and its complement multiplies the squared normalised spherical distance, and the same g_i reappears as the weight of the Karcher step that moves each codebook point; therefore the behaviour statistic decides the metric an item is measured in and the geometry decides where the codes it is measured against end up. Setting g_i = 0.5 removes the behaviour term from both the assignment and the codebook estimator; setting k_H, k_S -> 0 replaces both curved distances and both exp/log maps by their Euclidean limits, which changes the same assignment and the same codebook update.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If per-item behaviour tree-likeness is a real signal, then items whose training transitions are strongly cyclic are currently being forced into a hierarchy their behaviour does not have, and giving them a spherical fibre should (a) reduce prefix collisions between behaviourally distinct items in the tail, (b) lower the Stage 3 generator's cross-entropy on tokens 2 and 3 relative to token 1, and (c) raise Stage 3 test recall@10 above 0.065 in the single run. It is worth keeping if and only if the run both beats 0.065 and shows level-1 token usage that tracks the behaviour communities rather than collapsing onto a few radial shells.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the RQ-VAE quantizer, simultaneously in (i) the per-level nearest-code assignment metric and (ii) the Frechet/Karcher update of every codebook entry, i.e. in the core of Stage 2, not in an auxiliary loss.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: A trainable mixed-curvature product: Poincare ball of curvature k_H < 0 (initialised at -1) with the arcosh distance and exp0/log0 maps, multiplied with a sphere of curvature k_S > 0 (initialised at +1) with the arccos geodesic distance; both factor distances are renormalised by their own derived maximum.
ideas.key_change: The RQ-VAE codebook stops being a set of vectors in one Euclidean (or one Poincare) space and becomes a set of product-manifold points (a ball point, a sphere point) per level, with each item's assignment distance being a behaviour-weighted combination of the Poincare distance in the first factor and the spherical geodesic distance in the second. The same behaviour weight also enters the Frechet/Karcher codebook estimator, so the per-item tree-likeness statistic changes both which code an item gets and where the code sits.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The graph is built only from the training split sequences that the RQ-VAE is fitted on; validation and test sequences are never read, and no Stage-3 statistics (no prefix counts, no token frequencies, no popularity from the evaluation period) enter g_i, the codebooks or the curvature. g_i is a deterministic function of training transitions frozen before the first gradient step, so no validation or test interaction can influence an SID.
ideas.motivation: A single negative-curvature SID model assumes the item transition graph is a tree: one radial "is-a / sequel-of" depth plus an angular sector. Real consumption is a mixture. Sequel and attribute chains are tree-like, but repeat consumption, substitutes and mutually linked co-consumption form short cycles, and a Poincare ball can only represent a cycle by spending radial depth, which pushes cyclically consumed items onto the boundary where the metric is numerically hostile and where their prefixes collide with unrelated leaf items. The result is SIDs whose first tokens mix two incompatible kinds of neighbourhood, so the Stage 3 generator sees a prefix whose next-token distribution is a superposition of a hierarchy move and a lateral move, which is exactly the regime where prefix prediction degrades. The proposal gives each item its own curvature mixture, measured from its own training transitions, so the partition can be hierarchical where the behaviour is hierarchical and lateral where the behaviour is lateral.
ideas.novelty: Earlier mechanisms here either weight/diffuse the assignment mass (cocond-markov-poincare-ot), place a hierarchy in one negative-curvature latent (BRANCHCURV-SID, KAPPA_BRANCH, GEO-SHELL-RQ, CURVCELL-SID, SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ), transport successor directions in the tangent space (fork-angle-transport, fork-angular-barycenter, SUCC-TAN-RQ), use geodesic charts/anchors, or use a Lorentz cone. None uses a positive-curvature factor at all, none uses a product of two manifolds of opposite curvature, and none makes a measured per-item behaviour statistic choose the metric an item is quantized under. Here the behaviour statistic is not a weight on a distance and not a target shift: it is the mixing coordinate between a hyperbolic and a spherical metric, so removing it collapses to an unweighted product metric and removing curvature collapses to a plain weighted Euclidean quantizer.
ideas.observables: (1) SID assignment: adjusted mutual information between the level-1 token index and a held-out-free behaviour community labelling of the transition graph, plus the distribution of Poincare radii of level-1 codes (should stop pushing cyclic items to the boundary). (2) Gradient/parameter: the learned k_H and k_S should move away from their 1.0 initialisation and their ratio should correlate with the mean g_i of the items assigned to each level-1 code. (3) Prefix behaviour predictability: Stage 3 per-token accuracy and cross-entropy at token 1 vs tokens 2-3, and the number of distinct next-items sharing a 2-token prefix. (4) Stage 3 test recall@10, the judgement, against the recorded baseline and the 0.065 target.
risks: C_i is noisy for low-degree items, which are the majority of the long tail, so g_i may be near its 0.5 prior for most items and the mechanism may act only on the head; the spherical factor may simply add an uninformative rotational degree of freedom that the decoder ignores, in which case tokens 2-3 get noisier; the two curvature scales interact with the straight-through temperature, and although the temperature is inherited unchanged, a badly conditioned initial ball radius can make the arcosh term dominate early; and a gain could come from the extra geometry with zero contribution from behaviour, which the diagnostics must expose rather than the run hiding.
ideas.safeguards: clamp the ball radius ||p||, ||A|| to (1 - 1e-3)/sqrt(k_H) before every arcosh so the argument is >= 1 + 1e-7; clamp the arccos argument to [-1 + 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6]; guard ||zhat_S|| with max(., 1e-8) and skip the spherical term (g_i -> 1) when the norm is degenerate; parametrise k = softplus(k_raw) + 1e-3 and clamp k <= 1e3 so the Euclidean limit is reachable without division by zero; freeze g_i (no gradient) and assert it is finite and in [0.1, 0.9]; fall back to the Euclidean mean for any Karcher step whose denominator is below 1e-8 or whose result is non-finite; keep D_Hmax/D_Smax recomputed from the current curvature each step so the normalisers cannot go stale; reuse the baseline temperature, clip bounds and learning rate unchanged so no new constant requires tuning; assert one-hot/argmin consistency once per epoch and abort the level rather than emit NaN SIDs.
ideas.spec_equations: 1) g_i = clip(1 - C_i, 0.1, 0.9), C_i = c_i / (k_i (k_i - 1)), g_i = 0.5 if k_i < 5. 2) p = exp0^{k_H}(zhat_H) = tanh(sqrt(k_H)||zhat_H||) * zhat_H / (sqrt(k_H)||zhat_H||), q = R_S zhat_S / max(||zhat_S||, 1e-8), R_S = 1/sqrt(k_S). 3) d_H and d_S as in COUPLING EQUATION, with D_Hmax = (1/sqrt(k_H)) arcosh(1 + 2 rho^2/((1-rho^2)^2)) at rho = 1 - 1e-3 and D_Smax = pi R_S. 4) s_ik = softmax_k(-D_ik^2 / tau) with the baseline tau; hard = onehot(argmin_k D_ik); st_ik = hard + s_ik - s_ik.detach(). 5) zhat_H += sum_k st_ik log0^{k_H}(A_lk), zhat_S += sum_k st_ik (B_lk - q); loss as baseline on Dec(zhat) plus the baseline commitment term. 6) A_lk <- exp0^{k_H}( (sum_i s_ik g_i log0^{k_H}(p_i)) / max(sum_i s_ik g_i, 1e-8) ), B_lk <- R_S normalise( sum_i s_ik (1-g_i) q_i ); one Karcher iteration per step. 7) At inference the SID of an item is the triple of argmin indices, one per level, exactly as the baseline.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: encoder output z (d dims) per item, the frozen per-item behaviour weight vector g (24556 floats), the product codebooks {(A_l, B_l)}_{l=1..3}, trainable k_H_raw, k_S_raw, the baseline temperature tau. Outputs: for every item a 3-tuple of codebook indices (its SID), the straight-through product quantization zhat fed to the decoder, the commitment/decoder losses, and the gradient with respect to the encoder, the product codebooks and both curvatures.

specification.text: Precompute once on the Stage-2 training sequences only. Add a directed edge u_t -> u_{t+1} for every consecutive pair inside every training sequence. For item i let N_i be its out-neighbour set, k_i = |N_i|, and c_i the number of ordered pairs (a,b) in N_i x N_i with a != b and an edge a -> b; C_i = c_i / (k_i (k_i - 1)) if k_i >= 2 else 0 (this is the directed local clustering coefficient, i.e. how much i's successors feed each other = how cyclic/lateral rather than tree-like i's consumption role is). Define the tree-likeness weight g_i = clip(1 - C_i, 0.1, 0.9); if k_i < 5 set g_i = 0.5. The 0.1/0.9 clip and the 0.5 low-degree prior are fixed documented defaults, not tuned. At every RQ level l in 1..3 the encoder output z in R^d is split into z_H in R^{d_H} (d_H = ceil(d/2)) and z_S in R^{d_S} (d_S = d - d_H); the running reconstruction zhat starts at 0; p = exp0^{k_H}(zhat_H) is a Poincare ball point and q = R_S * zhat_S/||zhat_S|| is a point on the sphere of radius R_S = 1/sqrt(k_S); codebook entry k of level l is (A_lk, B_lk) with ||B_lk|| = R_S; the assignment uses D_ik = sqrt( g_i * dtil_H(p, A_lk)^2 + (1 - g_i) * dtil_S(q, B_lk)^2 ) with both factor distances normalised by their own derived maximum so that g_i is a genuine mixing coordinate; the straight-through code is the baseline's, with the baseline temperature reused unchanged; after choosing k*, zhat_H += log0^{k_H}(A_lk*) and zhat_S += B_lk* - q_base where q_base is the unnormalised zhat_S, i.e. the spherical factor advances by the chord to the chosen sphere point while the hyperbolic factor advances by the tangent image of the chosen ball point; the decoder and the commitment loss see zhat exactly as in the baseline. k_H and k_S are trainable via k = softplus(k_raw) + 1e-3, initialised at k_H = k_S = 1.0 (unit curvature, documented default). Codebook entries are updated by one Karcher/Frechet step per level with the same g_i: A_lk <- exp0^{k_H}( sum_i s_ik g_i log0^{k_H}(p_i) / sum_i s_ik g_i ), B_lk <- R_S * normalise( sum_i s_ik (1 - g_i) q_i ), where s_ik is the soft assignment mass of item i to code k.

ideas.title: Behaviour-gated mixed-curvature product codebook: each item is quantized under a Poincare factor or a spherical factor according to how tree-like its training transition neighbourhood is

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: w_i = 1 for every i, so the update is the uniform Poincaré Fréchet mean with curvature and eta unchanged; commitment is unweighted.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full update above, successor weights inside the Poincaré Fréchet step with weighted commitment; this is the only arm actually trained in the round.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: exp/log/d_kappa replaced by identity and squared L2, so the update becomes c_k ← c_k + eta * sum_i w_i (z_i - c_k) / sum_i w_i (weighted Euclidean EMA) with the behaviour weights kept.
ideas.behavior_computation: Built exclusively from the Stage2 training split. For every train session, for every consecutive pair (u -> v) with u != v, increment n_uv; then indeg_v = sum_u n_uv, n_v = number of train interactions of v, and w_v = (indeg_v + 1) / (n_v + 2); clip to [0.25, 4] and normalise to batch mean 1. The table is keyed by train item id only.
ideas.behavior_signal: Popularity-adjusted directed successor attraction (smoothed in-degree rate) of each item, from session-level directed transitions.
ideas.cost_estimate: One-off transition counting over train sessions, O(number of train transitions), under 2 s. Per step at the frozen scale (B = 1024, L = 3, d = 64): one extra Poincaré exp/log pair over B*L*d ≈ 2e5 floats plus one scatter-add, about 3–6% of step time, and a weighted commitment that is negligible. Across 3000 epochs x 24 steps = 72000 steps this is roughly +5–10% Stage2 wall clock, with no extra forward or backward pass and only a detached tangent buffer of B*L*d floats in memory.
ideas.coupling_equation: c_k ← exp^kappa_{c_k}( eta * sum_{i in S_k} w_i * log^kappa_{c_k}(z_i) / sum_{i in S_k} w_i ), where w_i is the successor-attraction weight and exp/log are the kappa = -1 Poincaré maps.
ideas.coupling_path: Item latent z_i → Poincaré log map at slot centre c_k → multiplied by the successor-attraction weight w_i → weighted tangent average m_k → Poincaré exp map back to the ball → the new slot c_k → next step's nearest-slot assignment and the emitted SID. Removing w_i makes the average uniform; removing curvature makes the same average a Euclidean weighted EMA. Either removal changes the slot, hence the SID assignment, in the same single pathway.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If successor-attracting items share codebook slots, then level-1 and level-2 prefixes become behaviourally predictive and the Stage3 generator's prefix-constrained decoding proposes better candidates, lifting test Recall@10 above 0.065. It is worth keeping only if the weighted Fréchet displacement concentrates on high-w slots, prefix→successor conditional entropy on train sequences falls relative to the unweighted codebook, and the Recall@10 gain is concentrated on high-w and high-predecessor-concentration items rather than spread uniformly.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Stage2 RQ-VAE training, inside the residual quantizer's codebook update rule together with its assignment and commitment, at every one of the 3000 epochs; the frozen codebooks then define the SIDs consumed by Stage3.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Fixed negative curvature kappa = -1 Poincaré ball: exponential and logarithmic maps at the slot centre, and the Poincaré distance d_kappa, used in the codebook Fréchet update, the assignment and the commitment term.
ideas.key_change: Replace the RQ-VAE codebook EMA/gradient update with a per-slot Poincaré Fréchet step whose per-item weights are the training-only, popularity-adjusted successor attraction of each item, and use the same weights inside the commitment term so the encoder and the codebook are pulled by one weighted geodesic objective.
ideas.leakage_boundary: SID construction reads only train item latents, train sessions and the train item set. The transition table, the weights and the resulting codebooks are frozen when Stage2 ends; no validation interaction, no test interaction, no Stage3 decoder feedback and no validation-derived constant enters w or C. The Stage3 protocol and its split boundary are unchanged.
ideas.motivation: The SID vocabulary is not the encoder, it is the codebook. Standard RQ-VAE trains every item latent with equal weight, so codebook slots are spent on popular but behaviourally interchangeable items, and the first prefixes do not separate items that actually follow one another. Directed successor flow is the cheapest evidence of which items deserve to share a slot or a prefix, yet it currently never reaches the estimator that produces the codebook.
ideas.novelty: Earlier rounds placed behaviour and curvature in the assignment step (Poincaré-cost Sinkhorn, successor-fork angles, cones, shells, geodesic charts, target transport). This proposal leaves the assignment cost untouched and instead changes the estimator that produces the codebook itself: every slot is moved by a weighted Riemannian Fréchet step in the Poincaré ball, so the SID vocabulary is learned, not merely assigned, under a curved behaviour-weighted objective. No OT, no fork angle, no cone, no shell, no per-prefix curvature.
ideas.observables: Which items share the first two prefixes; per-slot weighted tangent mean m_k and its norm; slot-centre trajectories across epochs; prefix→successor conditional entropy computed on train sequences; RQ-VAE reconstruction error; Stage3 test_recall@10 against the 0.065 target.
risks: The Fréchet step can be unstable or collapse several slots onto one high-w region; the weights can degrade into a popularity proxy if indeg and n_v are too collinear; codebook drift can hurt reconstruction and therefore the generator's conditioning; a single eta = 1 step is only a first-order approximation of the weighted Fréchet mean and may lag; the gain may be smaller than single-run seed noise.
ideas.safeguards: Clamp z_i to radius (1 - 1e-3)/sqrt(|kappa|); clamp the log-map argument strictly inside the ball; skip slots whose weight sum or support is below 1e-6; never move dead slots; detach z and c in the codebook update; run exp/log in fp32; renormalise after each exp so ||c|| <= (1 - 1e-4)/sqrt(|kappa|); NaN/Inf guard skips the slot update and logs it; eta = 1, weight clip 4 and kappa = -1 are documented defaults, never tuned.
ideas.spec_equations: z = exp_0^kappa( tanh(||e||) * e / (||e|| * sqrt(|kappa|)) ); for l in 1..3: a = argmin_k d_kappa(z, c_{l,k}); L += w * d_kappa(z, sg[c_{l,a}])^2 (+ reconstruction); r = log^kappa_{c_{l,a}}(z); for each k: S_k = {i : a_i = k}; if sum_{i in S_k} w_i > 1e-6 then c_{l,k} = exp^kappa_{c_{l,k}}( sum_i w_i * log^kappa_{c_{l,k}}(z_i) / sum_i w_i ); z = exp^kappa_{c_{l,a}}(r).
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs are encoder latents e_i, the train-only transition counts n_uv, the current codebooks C_l, beta from the baseline, kappa = -1, eta = 1. Outputs are updated codebooks C_l (hence the SIDs), plus logged per-slot m_k, ||m_k|| and the number of assigned items per slot.

specification.text: Fixed curvature kappa = -1 (documented default, never swept). Encoder emits e_i in R^d; map to the ball as z_i = exp_0^kappa( tanh(||e_i||) * e_i / (||e_i|| * sqrt(|kappa|)) ), which lands strictly inside the ball. For each residual level l = 1..3 with codebook C_l = {c_{l,k}} subset B^d: assignment a_l(i) = argmin_k d_kappa(z_i, c_{l,k}); commitment L_l = sum_i w_i * d_kappa(z_i, sg[c_{l,a(i)}])^2 plus reconstruction as in the baseline. Codebook update, per step, per level, for each slot k with S_k = {i : a(i) = k}: m_k = sum_{i in S_k} w_i * log^kappa_{c_k}(z_i) / sum_{i in S_k} w_i ; c_k <- exp^kappa_{c_k}( eta * m_k ), eta = 1. Residual r_i = log^kappa_{c_{l,a(i)}}(z_i) is fed to level l+1 as usual. Behaviour weights, training split only: count directed adjacent pairs (u -> v) inside train sessions, indeg_v = sum_u n_uv, n_v = train interaction count of v, w_v = (indeg_v + 1) / (n_v + 2) (Beta(1,1) posterior mean, in (0,1]), clip to [0.25, 4], then per-batch normalise w_hat_i = w_i / mean_batch(w). The codebook update is detached (sg), so it is an estimator, not a gradient path; the encoder still gets gradients through d_kappa and the commitment term. Self-transitions are removed before counting.

findings.detail: No defect in this area. The state that must be equal is equal, and it is equal by construction rather than by luck: the only writer of the codebook in the loop is the reduced Fréchet step, and the only writer at init is an explicit rank-0 broadcast. The `_last` cache is not shared state in the harmful sense (it is per-rank input to a sum that is reduced before use). One nuance, deliberately not reported as a defect: `weight_of` divides by the *per-rank* batch mean (frechet_poincare.py:141), so the effective weight of an item is `w_i / mean(w over its rank shard)` rather than `w_i / mean(w over the 4096-item global batch)`. That is exactly the proposal's own "per-batch normalise" rule applied to the rank's batch; the shards are random subsets of a shuffled order so `m_r ≈ m`, the reduced direction stays the correct weighted mean up to an O(1/sqrt(1024)) shard-mean fluctuation, and the codebook remains bit-identical on every rank because all ranks consume the same reduced sums. It therefore changes no rank symmetry and no correctness property of the mechanism.

papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.

findings.detail: the Möbius sum is written with a minus on the second term: numerator = (1 + 2c<xy> + c||y||^2)x - (1 - c||x||^2)y. The correct form (also the one in the repo's own model/utils.py:34) has + (1 - c||x||^2)y. With the minus, poincare_distance(x,x) = 2*atanh(clamp(2r/(1-r^2))) is not zero: 0.887 at r=0.2 and the clamped maximum 16.1 for every point with r >= 0.5. The map is also asymmetric and its order inverts: at r=0.5 identical directions give 16.1 while antipodal directions give 0.663. So the curved operation that the behaviour weights are coupled to is not the Poincare distance the proposal names: the argmin assignment prefers the code most anti-aligned with the item, the weighted commitment is minimised by moving the encoder away from its assigned code, and log_at/exp_at are no longer inverse maps (log_at(c,c) != 0), so accumulate/apply is not the weighted Frechet mean either.

findings.detail: The derivative, not the forward value: write r = tanh(|v|/2) = |exp_0(v)|. For a step that only changes the radius, d d_kappa/d|v| = [1/(1-r^2)] * dr/d|v| with dr/d|v| = (1-r^2)/2, so the metric factor cancels and the pullback derivative of d_kappa(exp_0(v), c) with respect to v is O(1) (the composition is 1-Lipschitz up to the constant), and d(d^2) grows only like 2*d (d <= 2*atanh(0.9999) ~ 9.9 for interior points). For tangential directions the same cancellation holds because exp_0's Jacobian carries the 1/(1-r^2) factor diagonally. Hence the commitment cannot blow up through the exp_0 map, and it does not vanish either: tanh's saturation is exactly compensated, so the encoder keeps a non-zero pull towards the assigned slot up to the boundary. Two bounded safeguards exist: poincare_distance caps the artanh argument at 1-1e-7 (distance hard-capped at ~16.1, computed in float64 so the cap is not reached in float32 precision), and clamp_ball at BALL_EPS=1e-4 makes the only uncancelled path: if |v| ever exceeds 2*atanh(1-1e-4) ~ 9.90 the clamp rescales the point, the metric factor 1/(1-r^2) ~ 5e3 survives, and the per-item commitment gradient becomes ~2*d*5e3 ~ 1e5*beta*w_hat, which clip_grad_norm_(1.0) would then scale down, dominating that step. This is a boundary that the frozen initialisation (Xavier on the 128->32 output layer, latent norms O(1), r ~ 0.2-0.5) does not approach, and the commitment pulls the point inward rather than pushing it out, so no systematic drift to the boundary exists. Also all non-differentiable arithmetic (accumulate/apply) is inside no_grad, and index_add_ weights are per-item scalars, so no inf/nan can be produced: mobius_add clamps its denominator at 1e-12 and every map is finite at the cap. findings.detail: The level-2/level-3 codebook initialisation applies the Poincare distance to a point that is not in the ball. `VQLayer.init_codebook` receives `x` = the residual handed in from the previous level, which at level 1 is the raw encoder output in R^d and at levels 2-3 is a tangent residual `x - log_0(code)`. It then does `embed_ind = torch.argmin(self.frechet.distances(x, self.get_code_embs()), dim=-1)` where `distances` (curvature on) evaluates `poincare_distance(x.unsqueeze(1), codebook.unsqueeze(0))`, i.e. it treats that unbounded tangent vector as a point of B^d. All 256 distances tie, `torch.argmin` returns 0, so every item is assigned to code 0 at initialisation. The residual handed to the next level is then `x - log_0(c_0)`, a single constant shift for the whole item set, and the next level's KMeans is fitted to that shifted set; `_copy_init_embed` maps the large-norm centres through `exp_0` (model/layers.py:93), whose norm is `tanh(||v||/2)`, so levels 2 and 3 start with all 256 codes squeezed onto the boundary shell at radius ≈ 0.9999 instead of being spread over the ball.
